## Second lane has now hit the same ceiling — and reading the gate's own source changes what this decision is about

`domain:ui` execution seat, PM session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Three things arrived after filing: the second fork is now measured rather than predicted, the two forks turn out to have **different shapes**, and the gate's own provenance comments record **two prior re-pins of this exact ceiling for this exact reason**. All figures below are read from `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` on `origin/main` directly, not relayed.

### 1. The second fork is real — #7194 / PR #7400

Delivered, draft, red on `check:eager-closure` only. Measured against a control build of the base, in two halves:

| build | `framework` gzip | delta | gate |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| control (`a6e5f7050`) | 523,823 B | — | exit 0 (headroom 177 B) |
| **mechanism only** (renderer + tests, packs at base) | 523,823 B | **0** | **exit 0** |
| mechanism + ten-pack copy (`eacc55913`) | 524,243 B | **+420** | exit 1, over by 243 B |

### 2. ⭐ The two forks are NOT the same shape, and no single option resolves both

| | mechanism bytes | copy bytes | fits with copy deleted? |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| **#7210 / PR #7391** | **230** | 423 | ⛔ **No** — still 53 B over |
| **#7194 / PR #7400** | **0** | 420 | ✅ **Yes** — gate exits 0 |

⇒ **Option C (ship untranslated English, defer the ten packs) resolves #7194 and does NOT resolve #7391.** When I filed this card I had one fork and presented C as a single option; that was accurate for #7391 and is wrong as a general answer. Only **A** or **B** resolves both.

### 3. ⭐⭐ The gate's own header records this ceiling being raised TWICE, for this exact mechanism

Verified by reading the source, not inferred:

| re-pin | `framework` ceiling | what the bytes bought |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **objectui#6759** | 502,000 → **512,000** | *"user-facing diagnostic text, in ten locales, for two ordinary author mistakes that used to be unreported"* |
| **objectui#7173** | 512,000 → **524,000** (+4,671 B) | 38 keys in ten languages for the AI approvals inbox |

Both comments make the same observation the two blocked cards make now. On #6759:

> The CODE that fix added buys none of this chunk, which is why there was nothing to trim instead: `plugin-timeline` is lazy and is not in the eager closure at all, so the guard, the value speller and both refusal branches cost this budget **zero**. **Every byte of the growth is `packages/i18n` locale data**, which lands here.

And on #7173, explicitly naming it as a recurrence:

> The COMPONENT costs this budget nothing: `plugin-chatbot` is lazy and is not in the eager closure. Every byte is `packages/i18n` locale data, which lands in this chunk — **the same mechanism as objectui#6759's twenty strings above**.

⇒ #7400 is the **third** instance of a pattern the gate has documented twice: a lazy plugin's diagnostic costs the eager closure nothing, and its translations cost all of it. ⚠️ I record this neutrally. It is genuine precedent for A — and *"this ceiling has now been raised three times in a fortnight for translations"* is equally a reason to ask whether B is overdue. Both readings live in the same fact.

### 4. ⭐⭐⭐ The decisive reading: neither blocked card caused this — 98% of the headroom went to drift

`PER_CHUNK_BASELINE['framework']` is **514,863**, pinned at #7173's measured head. The ceiling is **524,000**.

| | bytes |
|:--|--:|
| headroom the gate was **designed** to carry at the last re-pin | **9,137** (0.10x the 91,136 B regression) |
| `main` today | 523,823 |
| ⇒ **drift since the baseline was pinned** | **8,960** |
| ⇒ headroom left | **177** (0.002x) |

**Drift has consumed 98.1% of the headroom this ceiling was deliberately given.** Against that, the two blocked cards ask for **1,073 bytes combined** (653 + 420) — comfortably inside the 9,137 the gate intended to carry, and roughly **one eighth** of what drift took while nobody was measuring.

⚠️ Both prior re-pins were made under the same condition, and both said so — #6759 at 1.8 KB left (0.02x), #7173 at 1,808 B left (0.02x). **Today is 177 bytes, 0.002x — an order of magnitude tighter than either occasion that triggered a re-pin.** #6759's comment names where this belongs:

> The drift itself, and that nobody could say which side moved it, is objectui#6631; this card does not close it and deliberately leaves the other two entries alone.

⇒ This is the third card in a row to pay for drift it did not cause, and the second to be blocked outright by it.

### 5. If option A is chosen, what it mechanically requires

Not a recommendation — the arithmetic, so the choice is costed. The gate enforces two constraints, both checked in `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts`: every ceiling must pass on the measurement in `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`, and its headroom must stay under `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES`. Re-pinning onto today's `main` plus both cards (523,823 + 1,073 = 524,896) at the file's own ~0.10x convention gives a ceiling near **534,000**, with the baseline moved to the fresh measurement in the same commit. ⚠️ That is a **~10 KB** move, not a ~1 KB one — because it re-pins the gauge onto reality rather than only buying the two cards their bytes. Choosing A while moving the ceiling by only the 1,073 bytes the cards need would leave the gauge exactly as stale, and the next card would be back here.

⛔ The gate also forbids the opposite move — *"Do not LOWER one below the measured figure to express an aspiration: this is a ratchet, and a ceiling under today's reality is a gate that lands red on `main`"* — so option B's payload shrink must actually land before either ceiling comes down.

### Status of the two blocked cards

Both parked, neither weakened, neither ceiling touched. #7210 / #7225 → `Blocked-by: #7399`, `Unlock-action: re-check PR #7391`. #7194 → `Blocked-by: #7399`, `Unlock-action: re-check PR #7400`. Standing-down comments on both PRs. #7400's Clause-② contract review is running **in parallel** at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so it is ready the moment this rules.

⚠️ Also surfaced by #7400's implementer and filed separately as **#7401**: a registration's `defaultProps.chartType` is inert on the SDUI path, so `scatter-chart`, `plugin-charts:scatter-chart` and `pie-chart` all render as two-series **bar** charts — which also means `widget-dom-leak-sweep`'s pie / donut / radar / scatter entries have been passing as bar charts. Unrelated to this decision; noted so it is not lost in it.

## Measurement refreshed against current `main` — the gap is byte-identical 7 hours and ~9 commits later

`domain:ui` execution seat, PM session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. ⛔ **Not a re-ask.** Both blocked PRs were carrying readings taken at 17:40Z and 18:25Z against bases that are now long superseded, and this card's whole argument is quantitative — so the numbers are refreshed rather than left to be argued from stale data. The options and the ask are unchanged and are not restated here.

### What I did

Updated both PR branches onto current `main` (a merge commit each — ⛔ no rebase, no force-push, so neither dev's checkout is invalidated) and let CI re-measure.

| | old base | new base |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PR #7391 (#7210 + #7225) | `a6e5f7050` | **`bf244f400`** |
| PR #7400 (#7194) | `0614b6df1` | **`bf244f400`** |

`bf244f400` is `main` including tonight's landings — #7212 (`6aeba673c`) and #7204 + #7224 (`bf244f400` itself), among ~9 commits.

### The fresh reading, from PR #7391's job log

```
✅ Console eager closure is 3178.9 KB gzipped across 48 of 516 chunks (budget: 3191.4 KB, headroom: 12.5 KB).
❌ 1 eager chunk is over its per-chunk budget:
   ✅ vendor-objectstack   926.1 KB / 944.3 KB ceiling (headroom 18.2 KB)
   ❌ framework            512.2 KB / 511.7 KB ceiling (OVER by 0.5 KB)
   ✅ ui-components        387.3 KB / 389.6 KB ceiling (headroom  2.3 KB)
✅ Ceiling sensitivity … ✅ Ceiling freshness: all 3 ceiling constants are unchanged
   on `main` since this checkout's base (bf244f400…)
```

⭐ **`framework 512.2 / 511.7, OVER by 0.5 KB` — byte-identical to the 17:40Z reading.** PR #7400 is red on the same per-chunk check on its own refreshed head (`15ad6a762`); I have not re-read its exact figure and am not quoting one I did not measure.

### Why the refresh is worth having rather than noise

Two things it establishes that the stale reading could not:

1. **The rebuild is real, not a cached artifact.** The `ui-components` chunk hash moved (`ui-components-Bd4e_cV4.js` → `ui-components-DHsni2p8.js`), so `main` genuinely changed underneath and the closure was re-weighed — and still weighs the same for `framework`. A delta of zero from an unchanged build would prove nothing; this one has a control.
2. **The ceilings have not been touched.** Freshness passes against `bf244f400`, and `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS['framework']` is still `524_000` with `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE` still `514_863` on current `main`. So nothing has been re-baselined out from under this card, and nothing has shrunk the payload.

⇒ The situation is not drifting toward resolution on its own. `main`'s headroom has stayed at roughly **200 bytes** all night while nine commits landed, which is the same fact this card was filed on — now measured twice, seven hours apart, either side of three of this lane's own landings.

⚠️ For completeness on the other side of the ledger: **all three cards this lane dispatched tonight were chosen for byte-neutrality and all three measured clean** — #7212 (0 files added/removed across 33 packages, `Bundle Analysis` green), #7204 + #7224 (eager closure delta **0** across all 48 chunks, with a differing entry-chunk hash as the control), #7115 (docs and `scripts/` only). None of them consumed a byte of the headroom this card is about.

## New evidence for this decision: a THIRD PR is now blocked, and this one reds on a +16-byte change

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. First post from this seat on this card — I have deliberately posted nothing here until I had something that changes the decision input. ⛔ No recommendation, ⛔ no request to raise anything, ⛔ nothing asked of the maintainer beyond the record.

### The count moved: #7391 · #7400 · now **#7442**

PR #7442 implements the ruled fix for #7178 (director seat, [5509025252](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7178#issuecomment-5509025252), option A, Clause ② no — a `min`/`max` measure over a date renders as a date instead of a raw ISO string). It is complete, its tests pass, and it is blocked here.

### ⭐ What makes it worth recording rather than just counting

CI on `5ad78fde`:

```
❌ Console Performance Budget                     Status: FAIL
  Aggregate closure ceiling        ✅ pass    3178.3 KB / 3191.4 KB
  Per-chunk ceilings               ❌ over its ceiling
  Ceiling sensitivity (headroom)   ✅ pass
  Ceiling freshness                ✅ pass
```

| chunk | before | after | ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `framework` | 523,823 | **524,402** (+579) | 524,000 — **over by 402** |
| `ui-components` | 396,598 | 396,088 (**−510**) | 399,000 |
| aggregate eager closure | 3,254,604 | 3,254,620 (**+16**) | passes |

**The change's true payload cost is +16 bytes across a 3.25 MB closure.** The aggregate ceiling passes; only the per-chunk ceiling objects.

The reason is mechanical: the `framework` group is defined by **path** — `apps/console/vite.config.ts:742`, `/packages/(core|react|types)/` — so any code moving *into* `packages/core` scores against that ceiling even when an equal amount leaves another eager chunk. This PR is a **relocation**, not growth: the ruling required reusing the list-cell date path rather than writing a second date convention, and `packages/core` is the React-free engine, so the shared `formatDate` / `formatDateTime` had to move down out of `packages/fields` — the same move objectui#4576 made for `formatDisplayNumber`. CI's own per-package table shows both halves independently: `fields` **61.71 → 61.26 KB** gz, `core` **2.32 → 2.42 KB** gz.

⇒ So the gate now reds on a change that costs the browser 16 bytes. That is a property of how the per-chunk ceiling **attributes** bytes, not a property of the change — and it is a different fact from "the chunk grew", which is what #7391 and #7400 demonstrate. Recorded here because it is the kind of input that could change which option is right, and it did not exist when this card was written.

### What this seat has NOT done

- ⛔ Not raised `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS.framework`, not re-pinned a baseline, not touched the budget script — a gate ceiling is this card's subject and the maintainer's call.
- ⛔ Not shrunk the change to fit. That would mean keeping a date convention inside `dataset-format.ts`, which is the second-convention failure the #7178 ruling and objectui#4576 both forbid — trading a governance blocker for the exact defect the card exists to prevent.
- ⛔ Not enqueued #7442; it stays draft and parked behind this decision.

Stand-down notes for #7391 / #7400 remain as posted (5513935838 / 5514186581) and are not repeated.

## ⚠️ ESCALATION — the 177 bytes are gone. `main` itself is now OVER, so this is no longer two blocked cards: **every PR in the repo is red on `Bundle Analysis`.**

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. ⛔ Not a ruling, ⛔ not a re-grade, ⛔ no ceiling touched. New measurement only — the decision this card asks for is unchanged; what has changed is that it is now blocking everything rather than two cards.

### The measurement

PR #7467 (card #7459, a `plugin-timeline` + `i18n` change) failed `Bundle Analysis` at 07:24Z. Read from the job log, ⛔ not from the summary comment:

```
✅ Console eager closure is 3180.1 KB gzipped across 48 of 516 chunks (budget: 3191.4 KB, headroom: 11.3 KB).
❌ 1 eager chunk is over its per-chunk budget:
  ✅ vendor-objectstack   926.1 KB / 944.3 KB ceiling (headroom 18.2 KB)
  ❌ framework            512.8 KB / 511.7 KB ceiling (OVER by 1.1 KB)
  ✅ ui-components        387.8 KB / 389.6 KB ceiling (headroom 1.9 KB)
✅ Ceiling freshness: all 3 ceiling constants are unchanged on `main` since this checkout's base (c1fe272ad).
```

⭐ **That number is `main`'s, not the PR's.** `apps/console/vite.config.ts:742` attributes the chunk by **path** — `/[\\/]packages[\\/](core|react|types)[\\/]/` — and #7467's entire file list is `.changeset/`, ten `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`, and three files under `packages/plugin-timeline/src/`. Not one path matches. A diff that cannot add a byte to the chunk measured it at 512.8 KB, so 512.8 KB is what `main` carries.

### This card predicted the mechanism, and it has now completed

> absent a decision, **the next lane to measure gets the room**.

There is no room to get. The progression, all from this checker:

| reading | `framework` | ceiling | headroom |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2026-08-31 (`e33b44796`) | 492.9 KB | 500.0 KB | 7.1 KB |
| 2026-09-02 17:40Z (PR #7391) | 512.2 KB | 511.7 KB | −0.5 KB *(that PR's own bytes)* |
| **2026-09-03 07:24Z (`main` alone)** | **512.8 KB** | 511.7 KB | **−1.1 KB** |

The third row is the new one and it is different in kind: the first two were a *PR* over the line. This is **`main`** over the line, with no PR's bytes in it.

### What entered the framework group — and it is a landing of mine

Diffing framework-group paths between the last passing measurement (`3804c222b`, PR #7464 at 07:07Z) and `c1fe272ad`, **exactly two files**:

```
packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.hiddenVisibleSynonymy.test.tsx  | +84
packages/types/src/base.ts                                                  | +33 −3
```

Both are **PR #7457** (#7088) — which **I reviewed, accepted and enqueued** on the finding that it was comment-only. That finding was right about behaviour: no declaration moved, no accept set changed, Clause ② genuinely no. ⛔ I did not weigh it for **bytes**, and `packages/types` sits inside this very chunk — a fact I had measured earlier in this same shift while analysing #7442 and failed to apply one PR later.

⚠️ **Stated as an open question, ⛔ not a conclusion.** #7457's own `Bundle Analysis` **passed** pre-merge. A test file under `__tests__` should not reach the console module graph, and JSDoc should not survive minification — so *how* 33 lines of comment become ~1.1 KB of shipped chunk is **not established**, and I will not guess it. Two readings are solid: nothing else entered that group, and `main` is over.

I have dispatched a **measurement-only** run to establish the mechanism. It writes nothing.

### What this changes for the decision

The options in the body stand. Three things about them are now different:

1. **The blocked set is no longer #7391 and #7194.** It is every PR in the repository, including ones that touch none of this — #7467 is a timeline refusal screen.
2. **Option C is now definitively dead.** It was already short by 53 B on the mechanism alone; against a chunk that is 1.1 KB over before any card's bytes, it is not a candidate.
3. **Option B changed character.** The body frames it as "shrink the eager payload so the two locale-pack cards fit". The current blocker is **not locale strings** — it is whatever `packages/types`/`packages/react` contributed. B is still the only option that fixes the proxy *and* the thing proxied, but it can no longer be scoped as an i18n-only lazy-load.

⛔ **A ceiling raise is still not this seat's to take**, and is now less attractive than when this card was filed: raising it to clear a regression whose *mechanism is unknown* would bury exactly the signal the gate exists to give. The gate's own text — *"do not widen it just to get a green check"* — is pointed at this.

⚠️ One further consequence for whoever rules: while `main` is over, **the per-chunk half cannot distinguish a PR that adds framework bytes from one that adds none.** Every PR shows the same red. Until this is resolved, that verdict carries no per-PR information.

## Addendum — a natural control from CI's own runs, no build required

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Adding one reading to my escalation above ([5522186641](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7399#issuecomment-5522186641)) because it arrived on its own and narrows the question. ⛔ Still not a ruling; the dedicated measurement is still running.

Four PRs ran `Bundle Analysis` this morning across bases that **straddle #7457's landing**:

| PR | base | what it changes | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| #7464 (#7129) | `3804c222b` — **pre**-#7457 | `packages/types` + `plugin-detail`, 9 files | ✅ **PASS** |
| #7468 (#7344) | `d88e20f55` — **pre**-#7457 | `packages/types/src/zod/` ×6 + twins + the parity ledger, 12 source files | ✅ **PASS** (closure 3179.0 KB) |
| #7467 (#7459) | `c1fe272ad` — **post**-#7457 | `plugin-timeline` + `i18n` only, **no framework path** | ❌ **FAIL** — `framework` over by 1.1 KB |

⭐ The asymmetry is the point, and it runs opposite to "the PR that fails is the PR at fault":

- **#7468 is a large `packages/types` diff** — six zod mirrors, their TypeScript twins, the parity ledger — and it **passes**, on a base that predates #7457.
- **#7467 touches no framework-group path at all** and **fails**, on a base that includes #7457.

So the variable that moves the verdict is **the base**, not the diff. A PR that adds nothing to the chunk fails; a PR that rewrites much of `packages/types` passes. That is what a `main`-side regression looks like from the outside, and it is three independent CI runs rather than one reading.

⚠️ Bounds, stated: this narrows the window to *"something between `d88e20f55` and `c1fe272ad`"*, which contains **#7453 and #7457**. It does **not** by itself single out #7457, and it does not establish a mechanism — a `__tests__` file should not reach the console graph and JSDoc should not survive minification, so the obvious story is still unproven. The isolation run (revert each candidate separately, rebuild, re-measure, and grep the emitted `assets/framework-*.js` for a distinctive phrase) is what will settle it, and it will report here.

⚠️ Operationally: **#7468 and #7464 pass only because their bases are stale.** Both go red the moment they are rebased or enter the merge queue against current `main`. No PR in this repo can land until this is resolved.

## ⛔ Correction — my own central inference above is weaker than I stated. A commit touching **no** framework-group path moved the chunk ~0.9 KB.

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Correcting [5522186641](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7399#issuecomment-5522186641) and [5522268764](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7399#issuecomment-5522268764) before anyone rules on them.

### What I claimed

> `apps/console/vite.config.ts:742` attributes that chunk **by path** … #7467's entire file list … not one path matches. A diff that cannot add a byte to the chunk measured it at 512.8 KB, **so 512.8 KB is what `main` carries**.

The path rule is real and quoted correctly. The **inference built on it is not sound**, and here is the reading that breaks it.

### The measurement that breaks it

| PR | base | framework | over by |
|---|---|---|--:|
| #7467 — adds nothing to the group | `c1fe272ad` | 512.8 KB | 1.1 KB |
| #7471 — **does** edit `packages/types` (+129) | `0246d116e` | 511.9 KB | 0.2 KB |

Between those two bases **exactly one commit landed**:

```
0246d116e  docs(plugin-report,docs): shrink UNGATED_DOCS by four — plugin-report README
           plus the last three .mdx entries (#7458)
```

Diffing that range restricted to `packages/core packages/react packages/types` returns **nothing**. Control on the same command: the range is non-empty — 5 files, +89 −19, in `scripts/` and docs.

⇒ **A commit that changed no framework-group source moved the framework chunk by roughly 0.9 KB downward** — and `511.9` still includes #7471's own `packages/types` additions, so `main`-alone at `0246d116e` is somewhere ≤ 511.9.

### What that means

The chunk's measured size is **not a pure function of framework-group content**. Chunk assignment is a whole-graph property — module ordering, boundary shifts, what else got pulled in — so a change outside the group can move the number. Therefore:

- ⛔ **"This PR touches no framework path, so the figure is `main`'s"** is a weaker argument than I presented. It remains *evidence* — a non-group diff is unlikely to add group bytes — but it is not the proof I called it.
- The conclusion that `main` at `c1fe272ad` was over is still well-supported (the aggregate, sensitivity and freshness halves all passed; only the per-chunk one objected, on a diff with no group paths). But "512.8 KB **is** main's figure" should read "512.8 KB is main's figure **as measured through that PR's build**".
- ⚠️ **Whether `main` is over *right now*, at `0246d116e`, is unknown.** It may have come back under. Nothing here establishes it either way, and I am not going to infer it from #7471's 511.9 for exactly the reason above.

### And the #7457 hypothesis is weakened by the same reading

My earlier note pointed at #7457 because it was the only framework-group change in the window. That is still true. But if a docs-only commit can move this chunk ~0.9 KB, then **"the only group change in the window" is no longer sufficient to identify the cause** — the window contains non-group changes that demonstrably move the number too.

⇒ #7457 stays a *candidate*, not a finding. The isolation measurement (revert each candidate, rebuild, re-measure, and grep the emitted `assets/framework-*.js` for a phrase from the JSDoc) is now the **only** thing that can settle it, and I have redirected that run to add a `main`-alone leg at `0246d116e` and to report every figure against its base SHA.

### Unchanged

⛔ No ceiling raise. ⛔ No re-run. The decision this card asks for still stands, and the options are unaffected — what changed is that one of my supporting arguments is thinner than I wrote it, and a ruling should not rest on it.

⚠️ For anyone reading the earlier comments: treat **"main is over by 1.1 KB"** as *measured at `c1fe272ad`, through a PR build*, and **"every PR is red"** as *observed at that time*, not as a standing fact about the current tip.

## ⭐ Decisive reading: two PRs on the **identical base** disagree by 0.9 KB, and the one that ADDS to `packages/types` measures **smaller**

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. New measurement, ⛔ still not a ruling. This supersedes the reasoning in my earlier comments (already corrected once in [5522362614](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7399#issuecomment-5522362614)) and it should change how the per-chunk verdict is read.

### The experiment

I merged `main` into PR #7467 so it would rebuild against the current tip. Its diff touches **only** `packages/plugin-timeline/src/` and `packages/i18n/src/locales/` — nothing matching the `framework` path rule. So on a shared base it ought to read `main`-alone.

Both figures below are from the jobs' own logs, both with `EAGER_CLOSURE_BASE_SHA: 0246d116e`, both with freshness ✅:

| PR | edits `core`/`react`/`types`? | `framework` | emitted chunk | aggregate |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|
| **#7467** (head `2a4240161`) | **no** | **512.8 KB** | `framework-9qePxIpU.js` | 3180.1 KB |
| **#7471** (head `afcb85788`) | **yes**, +129 lines | **511.9 KB** | `framework-D3HugwBd.js` | 3179.2 KB |

⇒ **Same base. Same ceiling. 0.9 KB apart. And the one that adds `packages/types` code is the *smaller* one.**

### What this rules out

- ⛔ **"#7467's figure is `main`-alone"** — the argument I built two comments on. It cannot be, because #7471 sits on the same base and reads something else. At most one of these is `main`'s figure and the path argument cannot tell us which.
- ⛔ **"the chunk grows monotonically with framework-group content"** — #7471 adds to `packages/types`, lengthens two `describe` strings, and adds a `superRefine`, yet lands 0.9 KB *below* a PR that adds none of that.
- ⛔ **"a re-run would settle it"** — #7467's chunk hash is **byte-identical** before and after the rebase (`framework-9qePxIpU.js` both times), which is the expected result for merging a docs-only commit, and confirms the build is deterministic *for a fixed input*. The variation is not run-to-run noise.

### What remains, stated as narrowly as the evidence allows

Something **outside** the `framework` path rule moves what lands in the `framework` chunk — plausibly chunk-boundary assignment, which is a whole-graph property. A diff elsewhere can pull a module in or push it out.
